Old load may overwrite newer saved-state display. No provider call or credential leak reproduced; backend settings authority remains separate.

findings.trigger: Rapid add/edit taps while activeOwnerId awaits, or active-owner lookup fails before opening goal dialog.

findings.trigger: Two valid persisted reminder identities hash to the same positive 31-bit platform ID.

Repair checks tuple identity yet schedules with the same colliding key; no allocation registry or conflict rejection observed. Concrete admitted collision pair and effect must be reproduced, not inferred as common frequency.

Actual Drift + native fake keyed by integer: create both, reconcile/restart/cancel one; assert other retained and statuses truthful. Keep exactID orphan cleanup, owner-change gates and ordinary idempotency.

findings.trigger: Cancellation or dispose occurs while cached final artifact verifier is awaiting, before a ready/recovered artifact becomes active.

Existing tests cover cancellation during partial verifier, not cached verifier. Already-active verified artifact is a separate no-new-activation case.
findings.proposedRegression: Real temporary valid final bytes and ready/missing row with deferred verifier: cancel/dispose then release; assert no new activation or completion event, truthful cancellation, subsequent uncancelled recovery succeeds. Retain fresh commit-boundary and diagnostics exactly-once tests.

findings.trigger: Runtime.close throws during scanner disposal with an initialized camera.
findings.expected: Remaining camera/native cleanup is attempted exactly once despite an earlier cleanup failure; lease/result invalidation remains immediate.
findings.actual: _dispose nulls runtime then invokes close before camera.dispose without finally; memoized failed dispose cannot later retry camera cleanup. LiteRt close similarly marks closed before sequential interpreter/delegate/options cleanup. Failure injection/native throw reachability requires G8.3 reproduction.
findings.proposedRegression: Inject throwing runtime.close and count camera.dispose through actual ObjectScannerUseCases; assert camera attempted once and error retained. Exercise repeated disposal/late initialization and native resource wrapper failure where injectable; no physical leak claim from fake.

findings.trigger: Application resources dispose while a screen-started benchmark awaits repository/openRuntime, or a benchmark request starts after disposal.
findings.expected: No unowned late native interpreter starts after disposal completes; in-flight benchmark resources settle/close before teardown, or explicit cancellation invalidates admission.
findings.actual: DeviceModelUseCases.dispose delegates only to downloadManager. benchmarkActive/openActive lack lifecycle guard/tracking; scanner.dispose only owns its _runtime, benchmark opens separate handles. Screen epoch suppresses display but does not cancel benchmark. Native sync runtime may limit interleaving during inference; awaits during admission are real.
findings.proposedRegression: Deferred repository/openRuntime and fake runtime through actual DeviceModelUseCases: start benchmark, dispose, complete open; assert bounded drain/cancellation and all handles closed, postdispose admission denied. Also cover route background stale display and ordinary CPU/XNN results.

findings.trigger: A WAV response reports a different nonblank engine from selected descriptor.
findings.expected: Actual provenance must match allowed route or fail closed before caching/playback/telemetry.
findings.actual: Header engine is checked only nonempty then replaced by hardcoded enum; actual backend emits omnivoice, factory default is VoxCPM. Matching enum validation downstream is bypassed. Deployment configuration not executed.
findings.proposedRegression: Synthetic wrong-engine responses through both clients and actual synthesized handler/factory; assert no falsely attributed playback/cache, correct matching endpoints retain behavior. No server call.

findings.trigger: Configured remote returns oversized or continuing WAV/error stream, or response arrives after public timeout.
findings.expected: Finite response byte budget and terminated stream/request work; timeout must not leave unbounded accumulating work.
findings.actual: Response.fromStream materializes entire body; Future.timeout does not cancel original future. Dynamic slot is released when public wrapper ends, not proof raw work ended.
findings.proposedRegression: Controlled streamed client boundary/over-bound/stalled/late chunks and cancellation counter; retain 401 retry/circuit/quota and no live requests. Mirror/legacy analogous risks dormant.

findings.trigger: Player starts underlying audio then its start acknowledgment fails; standard route falls back to native.
findings.expected: Stop/drain failed player before next route or report cleanupIncomplete and fail closed.
findings.actual: Adapter only retires completion on start error; handler propagates and orchestrator allows playback failure fallback without stop. Start-only facade may clear stop obligation. Physical partial failure not reproduced.
findings.proposedRegression: SDK-shaped player sets active then throws; compose handler/orchestrator/facade, verify fallback waits stop, stop error blocks fallback; preserve completion-owned cleanup.

findings.trigger: Old untagged global onPlayerComplete event arrives after interrupted playback and new subscription.
findings.expected: Do not accept old event as natural completion of new content.
findings.actual: take(1) new subscription accepts first global completion without utterance identity; generation only fences retired closures, unlike conservative native TTS policy.
findings.proposedRegression: Controlled SDK stream: startA stopA startB emit lateA then actualB; prove B completion not prematurely trusted. Document platform event contract/device pending; no acoustic claim.

findings.trigger: Old speak holds first handler stop; explicit stop/new speak completes through other stop invocations; old stop resumes.
findings.expected: Retired control chain must not stop newer audible generation.
findings.actual: Stop-all retains cancellation as first error but continues subsequent stops. Facade controlTail serializes explicit stop, not raw speak pre-stop sequence; original provider future need not drain before newer speak.
findings.proposedRegression: Use actual VoiceUseCases+VoiceOrchestrator with per-call deferred stop handlerA and recording handlerB; prove old chain cannot stop B after replacement playback; retain best-effort all-handler cleanup on genuine explicit stop failure.

findings.trigger: Formatting completion or truncating a sequence above max_length.

findings.actual: Completion template and EOS each contain im_end; overflow removes prompt tail including assistant header while retaining completion. Current stub tests assert contains marker/length, not exact template/boundary.
findings.proposedRegression: Pure synthetic tokenizer fixtures exact EOS count, short/long prompt and long completion, mask alignment and nonpositive length rejection; no training/model/network. Resolve intended truncation policy before fix.

findings.proposedRegression: Extract or intercept pure feature conversion with varying unmasked suffix after masked prefix, all-masked and zero-epoch cases; no GPU, dataset generation or research execution.

findings.trigger: An owner synchronizes SRS revision1, then records another first-answer review for the same word and sends the resulting revision2 cache.
findings.expected: The explicitly mutable SRS mirror and operation receipt must advance together under owner/revision checks, preserving local immutable answer authority.
findings.actual: Client reconstructs SRS entityId=wordId and increasing localRevision (drift_sync_store.dart2262-2287); actual recordAnswer/reopen oracle expects base1/result2 at learning_event_sync_test.dart1893-1913. Rules fieldSrsStatePayloadOk pins revision1 (728-760), fieldOperationMatchesSrsState requires absent entity/base0/result1 (1532-1545), and match denies all updates (1810-1816). Thus revision2 is rejected by source rules independently of lost-ACK codec finding REV09-01. Rules tests2423-2549 intentionally test create-only behavior; fake client ACKs mask this cross-layer disagreement. Source mismatch confirmed, emulator/runtime NOT RUN. Rules also omit payload.wordId==entityId; client _requireMutableSrsEntity6405-6411 fails closed before applying mismatched identity, so no local identity corruption claimed.
findings.proposedRegression: G8.3 bounded local emulator rules+actual recordAnswer/store/gateway-codec regression: revision1 create then revision2 update with linked receipts succeeds, replay exact-once, stale/gap/cross-owner/tombstone/extra-field and payload-wordId/entityId mismatch denied. Preserve immutable answers and local projection dominance. Do not deploy rules or weaken receipt validation.

findings.trigger: Firebase credential create/link succeeds, but sendEmailVerification fails before register returns.
findings.expected: Account UI/local owner/provider session reach an explicit recoverable consistent state; retry must not falsely repeat completed account creation.

AccountUseCases43-52 only binds after gateway returns, so its bind-failure signout is bypassed. RegisterScreen39-76 reports failure and remains on registration; repeated create may encounter existing account while provider already has a session and local owner remains old. Bootstrap reconcile827 runs at next composition, not this catch. Existing fakes never exercise Firebase post-create verification failure. Distinct from REV03-11, which starts after account.register returns successfully.
findings.proposedRegression: Inject SDK-shaped create/link success then verification-send failure through actual FirebaseAccountGateway+AccountUseCases/UI. Assert provider and local identity consistency, explicit verification recovery and repeat attempt behavior for anonymous link and fresh create. No live Firebase calls or deleting created user as an assumed compensation.

findings.trigger: Export owner archive under learning preview or injected build feature registry, with an inactive/expired feature override row for a feature whose build state differs from field defaults.
findings.expected: An exported field named effectiveState describes actual configured feature state at its snapshot or explicitly labels a different baseline.

Bootstrap454-456 wraps build registry in LearningPreviewFeatureRegistry and638 composes RuntimeFeatureRegistry from it; preview dailyContinuity hidden becomes enabled (learning_preview_feature_registry.dart11-15). Archive exporter receives database/time but no effective registry. Existing archive exact-field tests do not compare exported state against preview/custom runtime. No installed release flag claim.

Retain deterministic snapshot, owner/global-data privacy and archive schema compatibility.

findings.trigger: Active owner changes after consent use case resolves owner A but before its awaited repository mutation; old owner remains a valid local row.
findings.expected: A current-learner consent decision must be admitted for its intended owner at the commit boundary or rejected for retry after transition.
findings.actual: Use case34-46 samples time then resolves current owner and awaits repository.decide without generation/gate admission. Repository decide uses explicit owner/version transaction but no active-owner fence; it can change old owner consent and withdrawal intents after transition. Strong participation/sync authorizers recheck active owner later, so this is a local decision-attribution candidate, not a claim that unauthorized remote research was activated. Existing consent tests cover time/version/callback, not switch-before-commit. Separate from REV03-08 destructive confirmation race.
findings.proposedRegression: Real Drift two-owner fixture with deferred repository boundary: invoke consent accept/withdraw for A, switch active owner to B, release old call; verify intended owner admission semantics, unchanged unrelated consent/withdrawal/outbox and positive same-owner controls. Keep deny withdrawal independent of remote receipt availability; no research activation.

findings.trigger: Activity or process is recreated while ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT is pending, or after a document write but before finishExportFile. Ordinary orientation is handled by manifest configChanges and is not asserted to recreate it.
findings.expected: A surviving operation settles truthfully; recreated sessions can reconcile uncommitted created documents without silently reporting success or losing rollback authority.
findings.actual: pendingExportResult/pendingExportBytes/unsettledExportUris exist only in the Activity instance. A callback with null pending state returns without settlement; a new instance rejects finish for an old URI. No saved-state/reconciliation or destruction settlement is implemented. Process death also destroys Dart, so a hung surviving Future is not claimed for that case. Native reproduction remains required.
findings.proposedRegression: Native recreation and retained-engine versus process-restart cases around picker/write/finish; assert truthful Dart settlement, no unauthorized artifact retention, and cleanup failure visibility. Keep positive finish and cancel cases.

findings.trigger: A large owner export or a slow SAF provider is accepted.
findings.expected: Export remains responsive and has a bounded resource/cancellation policy; success is acknowledged only after the supported provider completion boundary.
findings.actual: Artifact is a full Uint8List with no byte ceiling in its contract or saver. Native onActivityResult writes the full ByteArray synchronously, flushes and closes before acknowledging. Large/slow work can block the Activity callback; no stream/chunk cancellation or admission bound. This is a resource candidate, not measured ANR/OOM.
findings.proposedRegression: Controlled slow provider and large bounded fixtures measure callback responsiveness and cancellation at write/flush/close; verify no success on close failure and cleanupFailed on deletion failure. Do not introduce arbitrary truncation.

findings.trigger: WideCharToMultiByte size query returns zero for invalid UTF-16 command-line input.
findings.expected: Conversion returns the documented empty failure result without a huge allocation or exception escaping startup.
findings.actual: Size query result is decremented before assigning unsigned target_length. Zero becomes UINT_MAX; on a 64-bit string whose max_size exceeds that value, resize attempts roughly 4 GiB before the second conversion error check. Actual native input/API/allocator behavior has not run.
findings.proposedRegression: Native invalid-surrogate and mocked size-query failure tests with allocation bound, plus null/empty/ASCII/Thai/supplementary Unicode positives. Preserve error result without accepting malformed encoding.

findings.trigger: WM_FONTCHANGE is delivered during a creation/destruction interval when the object is attached to HWND but flutter_controller_ is null.

findings.proposedRegression: Native lifecycle harness delivers font-change before controller initialization and during teardown; confirm actual dispatch eligibility, then keep normal font reload behavior.

No device or full gate execution occurred.

findings.trigger: Wrapper-level stderr fills its redirected pipe before the parent reads it.

findings.proposedRegression: Bounded fake child/wrapper failure producing enough wrapper stderr; concurrently drain and verify complete evidence/exit plus timeout-tree cleanup. Preserve ordinary child log behavior.
